Report_ID: CAPS-IV score change from baseline to treatment end
Title: A Randomized Sham-controlled Trial of 1-Hz and 10-Hz Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (rTMS) of the Right Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex in Civilian Post-traumatic Stress Disorder
Author: Leong et al.
Comment: The paper did not report change-score means/SDs for the synthesis-required combined active comparison. Per the synthesis contract, each arm's mean change was derived as treatment end minus baseline, and each change SD was derived as sqrt(SD_baseline^2 + SD_end^2 - 2×0.5×SD_baseline×SD_end), assuming baseline–post correlation r=0.5. Derived arm values were: 1-Hz change -12.47, SD 31.9057; 10-Hz change 4.56, SD 26.9671; sham change 9.90, SD 14.1561. The two active arms were then combined with standard pooled-group formulas, yielding n=20, mean change -4.8065, SD 30.2908. Hedges' g was derived for active minus sham change and equals -0.5383, so negative favors active rTMS. The paper itself reports Hedges' g=-1.07 only for 1-Hz versus sham, not for the required combined-active comparison. Although 31 participants were recruited, the Table 2 group headers used for the primary outcome total 29 (11+9+9); no values were inferred for the other two participants.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Combined active right-DLPFC rTMS (1-Hz and 10-Hz)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Double-blind randomized sham-controlled parallel-group trial with repeated measures
domain: PTSD treatment with noninvasive brain stimulation
Study Environment: Single-site outpatient/community recruitment; assessments and treatments at Vancouver General Hospital
Medium: In-person right-DLPFC repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation
interaction_type: Daily active or sham rTMS administered by an rTMS nurse
Participant type: Adults aged 19 to 70 with primary non-combat-related PTSD
Recruitment source: Psychiatry outpatient and community programs of Vancouver Coastal Health
Outcome measurement: Change score defined as treatment-end CAPS-IV minus baseline CAPS-IV; higher CAPS-IV scores indicate greater PTSD symptom severity
Outcome variable: CAPS-IV score change from baseline to treatment end

Report_ID: Change in CAPS-5 total score from baseline to week 5
Title: Deep Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation Combined With Brief Exposure for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder: A Prospective Multisite Randomized Trial
Author: Isserles et al.
Comment: The paper reports positive adjusted improvement (baseline minus post-treatment), whereas the synthesis defines change as post-treatment minus baseline; signs must therefore be reversed before synthesis (active −15.48, sham −19.05). Change-score SDs are not reported, and the supplied Results do not provide arm-specific baseline and post-treatment SDs from which they can be derived, so Hedges' g cannot be calculated from this report alone. Group n values are the randomized/safety-set arm sizes in Table 1 (60 and 65); the Results state that 91 participants reached week 5 but do not give week-5 counts by arm.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('SDI dTMS') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Design Type: Prospective multicenter randomized double-blind sham-controlled parallel-group trial
Country: United States, Israel, Canada, and Croatia
Medium: Deep transcranial magnetic stimulation using the H7 coil
interaction_type: Script-driven imagery immediately followed by active or sham stimulation
Participant type: Adult outpatients with DSM-5 posttraumatic stress disorder
Outcome measurement: Adjusted change in CAPS-5 total score from baseline to week 5 in the intention-to-treat dataset
Outcome variable: Change in CAPS-5 total score from baseline to week 5

Report_ID: Change in Clinician Administered PTSD Scale (CAPS) total score
Title: A sham controlled study of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation for posttraumatic stress disorder
Author: Watts et al.
Comment: The paper does not report change-score means or SDs directly. Per the synthesis contract, change was derived as posttreatment minus baseline: sham 61.7−72.3=−10.6; active 53.9−81.6=−27.7. SD_change was derived assuming baseline-post correlation r=0.5: sham sqrt(12.2^2+11.1^2−2×0.5×12.2×11.1)=11.6880; active sqrt(9.5^2+15.3^2−2×0.5×9.5×15.3)=13.3787. M_diff is active minus sham change (−27.7−(−10.6)=−17.1). The reported P=.009 is from a Mann–Whitney comparison; no test statistic is given. Intention-to-treat/missing-data handling is not explicitly described.
Content length: 10 sessions on 10 consecutive weekdays; 20 minutes per day; 4000 total stimulations
Recruitment source: Behavioral Sciences Service Line at the White River Junction Veterans Affair Medical Center
Outcome measurement: Clinician Administered PTSD Scale (CAPS), blinded clinician rating
Outcome variable: Change in Clinician Administered PTSD Scale (CAPS) total score

Report_ID: Total-CAPS score change from baseline to week 5
Title: Effectiveness of Deep Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation Combined with a Brief Exposure Procedure in Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder – A Pilot Study
Author: Isserles et al.
Comment: Table 2 reports positive 'Improvement' values (baseline minus post-treatment). To follow the synthesis definition of change as post-treatment minus baseline, the extracted means have been sign-reversed to -24.3 and -9.1; the reported SEs are unchanged. The ± values are explicitly mean SE, so they are stored as SE rather than SD. The paper labels this analysis ITT N=30, but the explicitly displayed group sizes elsewhere in the Results/Figure 2 are EXP-STIM n=9, NOEX-STIM n=8, and EXP-SHAM n=9 (sum 26); the manuscript does not provide ITT arm-specific Ns that sum to 30. Therefore the explicitly stated analyzed arm sizes of 9 and 9 are retained, and no SD or Hedges' g is calculated here.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('EXP-STIM: active mPFC DTMS after traumatic and neutral scripts') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); treatment SD derived from its reported SE (SD = SE * sqrt(n)); control SD derived from its reported SE (SD = SE * sqrt(n)); N-INCONSISTENCY: n_control(9) + n_treatment(9) = 18 ≠ n_total(30) — verify per-group Ns
Design Type: Randomized double-blind sham-controlled three-arm parallel-group pilot trial
Study Environment: Department of Psychiatry, Hadassah-Hebrew University Medical Center, Jerusalem
Medium: Deep transcranial magnetic stimulation using an H-coil
Content length: 12 treatment sessions over 4 weeks (3 sessions weekly)
Topic of Content: Traumatic and neutral script-driven imagery immediately before stimulation
interaction_type: Clinician-administered stimulation after recorded script-driven imagery
Participant type: Adults with PTSD resistant to standard treatment
Recruitment source: Newspaper advertisements and referrals from collaborating medical faculties and personnel
Outcome measurement: Mean change in total Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale-II score from baseline to week 5
Outcome variable: Total-CAPS score change from baseline to week 5
additional_group_ns: NOEX-STIM: active mPFC DTMS after positive/non-traumatic and neutral scripts, n=8; excluded because it does not match the planned active-versus-sham comparison under the same traumatic exposure procedure.

Report_ID: Change in clinician-rated PTSD symptom severity (CAPS-5 total score; post-treatment minus baseline)
Title: Theta Burst Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
Author: Philip et al.
Comment: Arm-specific change means were derived as two-week minus baseline: sham 39.4−47.4=−8.0 and active 38.6−47.9=−9.3. Change-score SDs were not directly reported and were derived using the synthesis-plan assumption r=0.5: sham sqrt(10.6^2+13.8^2−2×0.5×10.6×13.8)=12.5108; active sqrt(10.0^2+11.4^2−2×0.5×10.0×11.4)=10.7685. M_diff was derived as active change minus sham change: −9.3−(−8.0)=−1.3. The reported d=−0.12 is the paper's Cohen's d standardized to a pooled baseline SD and reflects the primary ANOVA; it is not a derived Hedges' g from these change-score SDs. Ns are the stated intent-to-treat group sizes; the paper defines ITT as randomized participants who received at least one iTBS session and used multiple imputation for missing data.
Design Type: Randomized double-blind sham-controlled parallel-group clinical trial
Content length: 10 business days (10 daily sessions) in the double-blind phase
Participant type: Veterans aged 18–70 with chronic DSM-5 PTSD
Outcome measurement: CAPS-5 total score; higher scores indicate greater PTSD symptom severity
Outcome variable: Change in clinician-rated PTSD symptom severity (CAPS-5 total score; post-treatment minus baseline)

Report_ID: Percentage reduction in Clinician-Administered PTSD Symptom (CAPS) score from baseline to session 5
Title: Exposure Therapy and Simultaneous Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation: A Controlled Pilot Trial for the Treatment of Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
Author: Fryml et al.
Comment: This result cannot contribute to the prespecified change-score SMD meta-analysis because the paper reports only percentage reductions and 90% CIs, not raw mean changes and SDs of change or post-treatment raw means/variability. Baseline CAPS means are reported in Table 2, but no post-treatment raw means or SDs are provided, so change scores and Hedges' g cannot be validly derived. The active estimate (55%) lies outside its printed 90% CI (18.5–53.5), an apparent internal inconsistency retained verbatim. The paper is also inconsistent about course length (5 weeks in the abstract versus 8 weeks in Methods); the PTSD result is specifically reported at session 5. Table 2 does not define whether its ± baseline values are SDs or SEs.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Active rTMS plus prolonged exposure therapy') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Design Type: Prospective randomized double-blinded active sham-controlled pilot trial
Study Environment: Ralph H. Johnson Veterans Administration Medical Center
Content length: Once weekly sessions; session 5 assessment reported
Topic of Content: War-related trauma from Operation Iraqi Freedom or Operation Enduring Freedom
interaction_type: Active or sham rTMS delivered simultaneously with prolonged exposure therapy
Outcome measurement: Percent reduction in CAPS score at session 5 relative to baseline
Outcome variable: Percentage reduction in Clinician-Administered PTSD Symptom (CAPS) score from baseline to session 5
